Electronic Health Records

Electronic health records — advantages, documentation in EHR, privacy and security.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List advantages of EHR over paper records
  • Describe safe documentation in EHR
  • Explain privacy and security of EHR

In simple words

Electronic health records replace paper charts with digital records. They improve legibility, access and sharing of patient information — but they must be used carefully to protect privacy.

EHR documentation should be accurate, timely and complete — just like paper records.

Advantages of EHR

Advantage What it means
Legibility No handwriting errors
Access Authorised staff can view from anywhere
Sharing Easy to share between departments
Decision support Alerts, reminders, drug interaction checks
Storage Less physical space needed

Safe EHR documentation

  • Log in with your own ID and password.
  • Document in real time or as soon as possible.
  • Do not copy-paste without checking accuracy.
  • Chart only what you did or observed.
  • Log out when finished.

Privacy and security

  • Access only records of patients in your care.
  • Do not share passwords.
  • Log off or lock the computer when away.
  • Report privacy breaches immediately.
  • Follow hospital policy and data-protection law.

🔴 Protect EHR privacy

Access only the records of patients in your care. Log out or lock the computer when away. Never share your password.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Charting — document in the EHR as you give care, not at end of shift.
  • Medication administration — scan and check against the eMAR.
  • Viewing results — check lab and imaging results promptly.
  • Privacy — do not discuss patient information in public areas.
  • Breaches — report any suspected privacy breach to the privacy officer.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. EHR advantages: legibility, quick access, sharing, decision support, less storage.
  2. Document in real time or as soon as possible.
  3. Access only records of patients in your care.
  4. Do not share passwords; log out when finished.
  5. Report privacy breaches immediately.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Do not copy-paste without checking accuracy.
  2. Chart only what you did or observed.
  3. Lock the computer when stepping away.
  4. Follow hospital policy and data-protection law.

📌 Memory trick

EHR security: “L-A-L” — Login with own ID, Access your patients only, Log out when done.

60-second revision

  • EHR = digital patient chart.
  • Advantages: legible, quick access, sharing, decision support.
  • Document in real time; chart only what you did.
  • Access your patients’ records only.
  • Lock computer, don’t share passwords, report breaches.

Test yourself

An advantage of EHR is:

Answer: B. EHRs are legible — no handwriting errors.

EHR documentation should be done:

Answer: B. Document in real time or as soon as possible after care.

Nurses should access EHR records of:

Answer: B. Access only the records of patients you are caring for.

When leaving a computer, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Log out or lock the computer to protect patient information.

If a privacy breach is suspected, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Report any suspected privacy breach to the privacy officer immediately.
